events.title: Avars and Persians begin their assault on Constantinople
events.description: Some 80,000 Avars and Slavs, allied with the Sasanian Persians, began a coordinated assault on the walls of Constantinople, defended by some 12,000 Byzantine troops. After a month of bombardment, with their fleets sunk, the attackers abandoned the siege.

events.title: The former emperor Romanos IV Diogenes is blinded
events.description: The former emperor Romanos IV Diogenes had agreed to resign and enter a monastery in return for his life, but the caesar John Doukas broke the agreement and had him blinded at Kotyaion. He died in exile soon afterwards.

events.title: Nur al-Din defeats and kills Raymond of Poitiers at Inab
events.description: During the Second Crusade, the Zengid army of Nur al-Din Zengi destroyed the army of Raymond of Poitiers, Prince of Antioch, and the Assassins of Ali ibn-Wafa at Inab. Raymond was killed, and Antioch's eastern border was pushed west.

events.title: Skanderbeg defeats an Ottoman army at Torvioll
events.description: Leading the League of Lezhë, Skanderbeg defeated an Ottoman army under Ali Pasha at Torvioll in Albania, attacking its flanks and rear with troops hidden in the woods. It was his first major victory over the Ottomans.

events.title: Globe Theatre burns down during Henry VIII
events.description: A cannon fired for a stage effect set the thatched roof alight, and Shakespeare's playhouse burned to the ground within an hour. No one was killed, and it was rebuilt the next year.

events.title: Spanish found Mission San Francisco de Asís
events.description: Franciscan friars celebrated the first Mass at the mission later known as Mission Dolores, as Spain expanded northward in California. The settlement grew into San Francisco.

events.title: The Daily Telegraph is first published
events.description: The Daily Telegraph and Courier appeared in London. Under new owners it soon became a penny paper and for a time had the largest circulation in the world.

events.title: Roger Casement is sentenced to death for treason
events.description: The Irish nationalist and former British diplomat was condemned for seeking German help for the Easter Rising. Despite pleas for clemency he was hanged in August.

events.title: Sampoong Department Store collapses in Seoul
events.description: The five-storey store fell in seconds, killing 502 people. Investigators found illegal alterations and ignored warnings, prompting reforms of South Korean building safety.
